en: Aspiration for Sukhāvatī,
translated by the Dalai Lama Gabchu Samten Darji,
a member of the Qingzi Jingshuan (Imperial Academy of Translators) serving at Fuyou Monastery.
Within the successive lifetimes of Śākyamuni, This prayer for rebirth in the supreme realm praised by the virtuous,
Is spoken with all my strength out of compassion; For those heavily obscured by the veil of ignorance,
The lives of gods and humans are mangled by the weapon of anger.
Bound by craving within the prison of saṃsāra, The waters of karma drift one into the ocean of the three realms of existence.
Washed and tossed about by the many waves of the sufferings of sickness and old age, One is driven into the maw of the sea-monster, the Lord of Death.
Constantly oppressed by the burden of unwanted suffering, One cries out in lamentation, a name for those without refuge and stained with disgrace.
May my vows and heart be witnessed by those who see: I pray with utmost sincerity before Amitābha,
Avalokiteśvara, Mahāsthāmaprāpta Bodhisattvas, and their retinues— those who guide the suffering and solitary—
to not forget the sublime vows you once made throughout many kalpas for our sake.
Just as the Lord of Garuḍas traverses the sky, may you descend through the power of your compassion;
we pray that the two oceans of provisions, which are the objects of aspiration for ourselves and others throughout the three times, [may be fulfilled].
May we all unite our strength as one support;
when we approach the end of our lives,
may we personally behold Amitābha coming to welcome us.
The two great Bodhisattvas,
together with their retinues, appeared before him surrounded by them.
At that time, he gave rise to a state of supreme, singular, and ultimate sincerity toward the Buddha and his assembly.
Yet there was no suffering of life being cut short;
he remained true to his faith and integrity,
as well as to the mindfulness of the realms he had perceived.
At the time of his passing,
the eight great disciples of the Buddha all arrived by means of their supernatural transformations.
They shall be guided along the path to Sukhāvatī.
Following these instructions, they will proceed directly to that supreme realm of Sukhāvatī,
emerging from within a precious lotus.
May they be born into the lineage of those with sharp faculties in the Mahāyāna.
At the time of birth,
may they possess all dhāraṇīs and various meditative concentrations.
The path of mind free from conditions,
inexhaustible eloquence, and so forth—
immeasurable and supreme virtues.
Having attained full completion,
they immediately take refuge in the unsurpassed guide, Amitābha Buddha,
as well as all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions.
They were all filled with joy and wished to receive the imperial decree of the Mahāyāna Dharma regarding the meaning of those various teachings.
In a single kṣaṇa, through rational integration,
one immediately mounts the unimpeded miraculous transformation and arrives at the Vaipulya Buddha-fields.
May I extensively practice the sublime conduct of a bodhisattva and may all vows be fully perfected;
and when I am born in the Pure Land, may it be so.
Arousing courageous compassion,
he arrived specifically in this defiled land by means of unimpeded spiritual transformations.
For the sake of all sentient beings,
he teaches according to the Dharma, each in accordance with their own individual conditions.
May they all be established securely in the pure path praised by all Buddhas;
may they universally practice rare and wondrous deeds,
and may all be swiftly brought to fulfillment.
May boundless sentient beings benefit;
may they all easily attain the fruit of Buddhahood.
May they, at the time of their death, be surrounded by the assembly of the ocean-like multitude as they attend upon Amitābha.
Clearly visible before my eyes, compassion and faith fill my heart;
as the signs of the intermediate state (antarābhava) appear, may the Son of the Buddha grant me instruction.
Once born in the Pure Land, I shall return to transform the beings of this defiled world.
May such a sublime realm as this be attained;
until it is so attained, I pray that in birth after birth and from lifetime to lifetime, [may I be born there].
Constantly encountering the Buddha's teachings,
they have realized the wisdom of hearing, contemplation, and cultivation as found within the various sūtras and śāstras.
May I obtain a pure body; having obtained that body,
may it be adorned with the seven virtues of the noble class.
May we never be separated.
Thus, at all times, may we remember our previous lives.
May I attain the knowledge of past lives;
in birth after birth throughout all ages,
wherever I behold the three realms of existence.
They all gave rise to thoughts of no benefit,
and regarding the merit of liberation,
they immediately conceived the intent to seize it.
Within the discipline of the Buddhas,
may I attain renunciation;
once I have attained renunciation, [may I...]
Untainted by any evil rebirths,
he perfectly maintains the prohibitive precepts.
Having proceeded to the center of the Gate of Limitlessness,
may I attain Great Bodhi,
just as the Great Bhikṣu Akṣobhya Buddha did.
Furthermore, throughout successive lives and births,
within all phenomena— both defiled and pure—
they will accord with reality and achieve harmonious integration.
The path of perfect realization;
the dhāraṇī that maintains the words and meanings of all phenomena without loss or forgetfulness.
May they obtain everything in full abundance,
just as they already possess it,
when they show it to others.
May I attain pure and unimpeded eloquence,
and furthermore, in birth after birth,
may I abide in the *Śūraṅgama* and other such samādhis.
May all beings fully attain, without exception, the five eyes beginning with the fleshly eye, and the six supernormal powers beginning with the power of miraculous feats.
Furthermore, in birth after birth throughout successive lifetimes,
by the power of their own innate capacity,
they will discern all paths of good and evil.
May I attain vast wisdom regarding the subtle distinctions among all phenomena, both defiled and pure.
May all be clearly distinguished as they appear,
entirely free from confusion or admixture;
may I attain the wisdom of sharp and clear insight.
All thoughts of non-realization, mistaken realization, and doubt,
at the very moment they are about to arise,
will be entirely extinguished without remainder.
May I swiftly attain the wisdom that perceives this;
may I attain the profound and secret wisdom through which the meaning of the wondrous Dharma-texts can be understood without the need for arduous study, as it cannot be measured by others.
In summary, this fully elucidates the faults of leaking secret wisdom,
as well as the textual meaning of the passage concerning the departure from wisdom.
Cultivating the practices for awakening through skillful means and correct wisdom,
may I reach the further shore in their entirety,
and may my vows be like those of the Honored One, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva.
In this way, through such vast, great,
and luminous [practice], one will swiftly perceive all profound and secret wisdoms,
all of which become easily attained.
According to circumstances, it upholds [the Dharma],
refutes heterodox teachings,
and is able to bring joy to the wise.
Relying on the Buddha’s teaching of all dharmas,
having skillfully analyzed, discussed, and compiled them,
may I attain the further shore as a wise one.
Furthermore, in life after life,
whenever they regard their own self-interest as paramount,
regarding the vast conduct of a bodhisattva...
If they arise and retreat,
they are all utterly severed and extinguished by means of a courageous mind.
They further diligently benefit others,
all reaching the other shore from the perspective of skillful means and bodhi.
Practicing the bodhisattva path,
may we all reach the ultimate limit,
and may our vows be like those of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, throughout successive lifetimes,
they practice the path that benefits both themselves and others,
and they utterly destroy all demons and heterodox teachers.
And when encountering various adversaries,
one cultivates the bodhisattva practice through skillful means and courageous strength.
May we all reach the ultimate consummation.
May we be like the Lord of Secrets, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
in birth after birth and life after life.
By means of diligence that abandons indolence,
one perfects the sublime conduct of a bodhisattva, from the first generation of the mind of enlightenment until the very moment of its completion.
Furthermore, being free from indolence,
one attains supreme enlightenment through great diligence.
May I, like the peerless Śākyamuni Buddha,
in birth after birth and life after life,
bring to rest and eliminate all interruptions in the cultivation of the path.
Regarding all ailments of body and mind,
by merely reciting this subtle title and name at the proper time,
one can immediately extinguish the pains and transgressions of body, speech, and mind.
May I be like the Tathāgata Bhaiṣajyaguru-vaiḍūryaprabha-rāja;
furthermore, throughout all successive lifetimes,
may my lifespan never come to an end when the time of death arrives.
By merely invoking this subtle title,
one can destroy untimely and accidental deaths;
may it be like Amitāyus Buddha.
When the time for the obstruction of one's lifespan approaches,
one will immediately behold the salvation of Amitāyus, who manifests his body in accordance with the karma among the four types of karma.
Thus they are tamed.
Having seen their bodies,
may the obstacles to their longevity be completely eliminated without remainder.
And at the time when that [Buddha] manifests his body according to their needs,
they immediately recognize him as Amitāyus;
because they have given rise to unwavering, firm, and sincere resolve, through the power of this, they attain it.
May they be born in all places and vow never to be separated from Amitāyus Buddha,
who shall personally act as their spiritual friend.
Furthermore, in birth after birth throughout all lifetimes,
they shall obtain the root of all mundane and supramundane merits.
May the spiritual friend who is fully endowed with the nature and characteristics of the Mahāyāna joyfully protect and sustain [me];
and whenever such protection is maintained, [may it continue].
In the presence of the spiritual friend and teacher,
may I give rise to firm faith that never regresses;
may I always remain joyful.
In a single moment,
may you not cause me displeasure;
for you have been pointed out to me by my spiritual friend and teacher.
In accordance with those various teachings,
may I vow never to fail to fully receive their taught meanings,
and may I assimilate them through correct reasoning.
And may they be able to practice it,
vowing to reach its ultimate consummation in a single instant.
May I never be sent by evil friends;
in birth after birth,
may I be one who reverently believes in cause and effect.
Furthermore, the mind of weary detachment and the sublime mind of bodhi,
along with pure vision, are all attained in complete harmony and integration.
Practice the conduct of effortless endeavor;
may it never be interrupted and arise in all places.
May all roots of virtue cultivated through body, speech,
and mind be dedicated entirely for the benefit of others;
may they serve as the cause for the attainment of pure enlightenment.
May I, until I have realized the wondrous and supreme fruit of that Blessed One,
obtain a body for the cultivation of the path that is pure; may I remember [the Dharma] in every lifetime and always leave the household life,
possessing eloquence, meditative concentration, supernormal powers, and mantras, upholding an infinite treasury of all meritorious qualities.
May I obtain as my peerless friend both compassion and wisdom, And swiftly cultivate bodhicitta until its ultimate consummation.
When the signs of untimely death appear in the heavens, And the body of Amitāyus Buddha manifests clearly before me,
Then may I sever the fierce power of the Lord of Death, And swiftly attain the lineage of the deathless.
May I have immeasurable life in every lifetime, And personally serve as a teacher of the Mahāyāna.
Within the principles praised by the Buddhas, May I never for a single moment fall into indolence or sloth.
May I never abandon sentient beings for my own benefit, Nor give rise to a mind of discrimination.
Cultivating the principle of benefiting others without confusion, through skillful means and wisdom, I have deeply benefited others by reciting this Honored One’s name with even a slight thought.
This shall eliminate all harms and the karmic fruits of transgressions, transforming them into causes for abundance and peace; it is a direct step upon the stages of the Supreme Vehicle.
The Buddha-sons bring about subtle signs of liberation; They extinguish the baleful influences that obstruct the bodhisattva path.
All necessities and provisions shall be abundant and harmonious; Whatever one subtly contemplates in the mind shall be perfectly accomplished.
Śākyamuni, Amitābha, and Maitreya, Mañjuśrī, Guhyapati, and Avalokiteśvara.
The Sugata’s retinue is the true causal condition; may this aspiration not be in vain, but be swiftly fulfilled.
[End of the Prayer for Rebirth in Sukhāvatī.]
